title: When the soul feels worn thin
issueStatement: You are still functioning, but the inner thread feels overused, brittle, and close to snapping.
centralInsight: Gurbani treats exhaustion as more than low energy. It can be the fruit of wandering, over-carrying, and trying to finish the path without Sangat, patience, or Naam.
practicalReflection: A tired soul often keeps adding movement. Guru keeps turning it back toward company, hearing, remembrance, and the right kind of rest.
actionPrompt: Shrink the day to one faithful practice instead of ten frantic ones.

source.shortMeaning: Search can exhaust the body until saint company and mercy cool it back down.
source.lifeApplication: Exhaustion is sometimes the cost of trying to settle the soul alone.

excerpts.explanation: The shabad names a tired form of searching that still does not land.

source.shortMeaning: Wandering ceases and patience becomes honorable where Naam is heard.
source.lifeApplication: The exhausted life may need less self-pressure and more listening.

excerpts.explanation: Guru pairs rest with hearing rather than with collapse.

source.shortMeaning: Repeated remembrance is given as medicine for worry and bodily strain.
source.lifeApplication: Exhaustion sometimes needs repetition more than innovation.

excerpts.explanation: The line is practical: remembrance changes what the body is carrying.
